newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar board approves cyclohexane plant.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar board approves cyclohexane plant.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp said its board on Tuesday approved the construction of a 25 million gallon per year cyclohexane plant at its Three Rivers refinery in South Texas.
The plant will start up in late 1998 and capacity can be expanded to 50 million gallons, chief executive Roger Hemminghaus told shareholders at the company's annual meeting.

A benzene, toluene and xylene (BTX) extraction plant, which upgrades gasoline components to petrochemical feedstocks, started up last week at Three Rivers and produced on-specification high purity benzene yesterday, Hemminghaus said.
The new cyclohexane plant will take the benzene produced by the BTX unit and further upgrade it to a raw material used in the production of nylon by Gulf Coast customers.
UDS will also construct a third polymer grade propylene splitter at its Mont Belvieu operations near Houston, Texas.
The one billion pounds per year splitter is scheduled to start operations in the third quarter of 1998.

Hemminghaus said that the new splitter, in conjunction with a 25 percent increase in the capacity of two existing splitters, will increase polymer grade propylene production capacity at UDS's Mont Belvieu facility to three million pounds per year. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
